bundles.name: Civil identity core
bundles.description: The registered identity itself: the anchor that other models reference, and the core attributes a registrar establishes and maintains about it.
bundles.rationale: UN guidance defines legal identity as basic characteristics conferred through registration; ISO/IEC 24760 separates the entity from the identity information held about it. The anchor plus its registered core attributes must therefore be one coherent, separately governed concern.

layers.name: Identity anchor and record identity
layers.description: What the person entity is, how it is uniquely referenced within a domain, and how multiple records claiming the same person are reconciled.

findings.name: Person identity anchor
findings.description: The natural person as a persistent entity distinct from any record, identifier, document or credential about them, carrying the reference identifier every other model points to.

findings.name: Duplicate detection, merge and split
findings.description: Several records may describe one person across systems; the model must express same-as links, merge, supersession and split without destroying history or silently unifying distinct people.

findings.name: Exceptional identity paths
findings.description: UN LIA explicitly covers persons whose birth was not registered and refugees whose proof of legal identity may be issued by the host State or an internationally mandated authority. Statelessness is a named UN LIA concern. National CRVS practice also includes foundlings, unknown parentage, incomplete dates, delayed registration and, in some jurisdictions, presumed death and later identity restoration. Those last national cases are recorded here as operating needs with incomplete global normative detail.

layers.name: Registered core attributes
layers.description: The attributes a civil registrar establishes and maintains: legal names over time, birth facts, and the administratively recorded sex or legally recognised gender.

findings.name: Legal name as a versioned structured fact
findings.description: Legal name is a time-bounded, structured, script-bearing fact with an ordering convention, not a fixed string attribute of the person.

findings.name: Registered birth facts
findings.description: Date, precision, place and, where recorded, time of birth as registered, plus multiple-birth order, distinguished from the place and date of registration.

findings.name: Sex and gender recording
findings.description: Administratively recorded sex, legal gender recognition and self-identified gender are three distinct values with different code lists, owners and disclosure rules.

bundles.name: Identifiers and evidence
bundles.description: Scheme-qualified identifiers assigned to the person, the documents and attestations that evidence identity, and the assurance produced by proofing.
bundles.rationale: ISO/IEC 24760 separates identifier from identity; UN legal-identity guidance treats documents as proof of a registered identity rather than the identity itself; NIST separates the proofing outcome from the resulting credentials. These three must be modelled as evidence about the anchor, never as the anchor.

layers.name: Identifier schemes and correlation
layers.description: How identifiers are assigned under named schemes with authorities and validity, and how their correlation properties are governed.

findings.name: Scheme-qualified identifier assignment
findings.description: An identifier attaches to the person under a named scheme with an assigning authority, validity period, format rule and reuse policy, without becoming the person.

findings.name: Identifier correlation and pseudonymity
findings.description: Cross-domain identifiers make a person correlatable across contexts; the model must record correlatability class and any pairwise or sector-specific pseudonym derivation.

layers.name: Identity evidence and assurance
layers.description: Issued documents and electronic attestations that evidence identity, and the proofing process that produces an assurance level.

findings.name: Issued identity evidence
findings.description: Physical documents and electronic attestations evidence a registered identity and assert a subset of attributes; they never constitute the person and their revocation does not revoke the person.

findings.name: Identity proofing and assurance
findings.description: The recorded outcome of resolving, validating and verifying a claimed identity against evidence, expressed as an assurance level with an expiry and an optional biometric reference.

bundles.name: Legal standing
bundles.description: The person's status in law: civil status, nationality or statelessness, legal capacity and any representation or support arrangement.
bundles.rationale: UN vital-statistics guidance makes civil status a registered legal fact; legal identity and nationality are the basis for document issuance; the CRPD constrains how capacity and representation may be recorded. Each is a separately governed legal state, not a demographic attribute.

layers.name: Civil status
layers.description: The registered civil or marital status, its effective date, governing jurisdiction and causing act.

findings.name: Registered civil status
findings.description: One current registered civil status per person with an effective date and governing jurisdiction; history is carried by the acts that changed it, not by overwriting the value.

layers.name: Nationality and statelessness
layers.description: Nationalities held, their basis and dates, and the distinct determination of statelessness or undetermined nationality.

findings.name: Nationality holding
findings.description: Zero, one or several nationalities held by the person, each with a coding, acquisition basis, dates and conferring authority.

findings.name: Statelessness and undetermined nationality
findings.description: Determined statelessness, undetermined nationality and simply unrecorded nationality are three different states with different consequences for document issuance.

layers.name: Legal capacity and representation
layers.description: The person's legal capacity state and any arrangement by which another party supports or acts for them.

findings.name: Legal capacity state
findings.description: Capacity is a time-bounded, domain-scoped legal state established by a legal act, with equal recognition before the law as the default and restriction as the evidenced exception.

findings.name: Representation and support arrangement
findings.description: An arrangement by which a person or organization supports or acts for the person, distinguishing supported from substituted decision-making and recording the person's own will and preferences.

bundles.name: Life course
bundles.description: The person through time: anchors to registered life events, the separation of occurrence time from record time, vital status and the lifecycle of the identity record itself.
bundles.rationale: Civil registration is defined as continuous recording of vital events from birth to death, with occurrence and registration consistently distinguished; ISO/IEC 24760 frames identity as passing through lifecycle states. Time handling is therefore a first-class concern, not an implementation detail.

layers.name: Life event anchoring and time
layers.description: How registered life events attach to the person and how occurrence, registration and ingestion times are kept apart.

findings.name: Vital and registered life event anchor
findings.description: The person carries typed anchors to life events resolved in the vital-event model, together with the role the person played in each event.

findings.name: Occurrence time versus record time
findings.description: Every person fact carries a time of occurrence, a time of registration and a time of ingestion; conflating them corrupts history and prevents lawful correction.

layers.name: Vital status and record lifecycle
layers.description: Whether the person is living, deceased or presumed dead, and which lifecycle state the identity record itself occupies.

findings.name: Vital status and death registration
findings.description: Vital status is an evidenced state; registered death, judicially declared death and presumed death are distinct and must not be collapsed.

findings.name: Identity record lifecycle state
findings.description: The identity record moves through governed states such as established, active, suspended and archived; transitions carry an authority, a reason and a timestamp.

bundles.name: Personal sphere
bundles.description: Data the person declares and controls: contact points, declared residence pointer, self-declared attributes and communication preferences.
bundles.rationale: UN legislative guidance and data-protection law both separate what an authority registers from what the person supplies about themselves. Mixing the two destroys the ownership boundary and misrepresents assurance.

layers.name: Contact, presence and declarations
layers.description: Person-controlled reachability, residence pointer and self-declared attributes, each explicitly flagged as unwarranted by any registrar.

findings.name: Person-controlled contact point
findings.description: A channel through which the person can be reached, owned and revocable by the person, with a verification state and per-purpose usage limits.

findings.name: Declared residence pointer
findings.description: A typed pointer to an address resolved in the place model, distinguishing legal domicile, registered residence and self-declared mailing address from statistical usual residence.

findings.name: Self-declared attributes and preferences
findings.description: Values supplied solely by the person, including communication and accessibility preferences, carrying no registrar warranty and always distinguishable from verified values in any projection.

bundles.name: Personal data governance
bundles.description: Lawful basis and consent, subject-right execution, minimal disclosure, retention, erasure and disclosure audit over person data.
bundles.rationale: Person data is personal data by definition; UN legislative guidance requires confidentiality and access control over civil-registration records, and EU law defines subject rights, special categories and storage limitation. Governance is therefore inseparable from the model, not an optional overlay.

layers.name: Lawful basis and subject rights
layers.description: Why each processing purpose is permitted, how consent is scoped and withdrawn, and how subject-right requests are executed.

findings.name: Lawful basis and consent grant
findings.description: Each processing purpose is bound to a lawful basis; consent-based purposes carry a scoped, withdrawable grant, while statutory registration processing is not consent-dependent.

findings.name: Subject right execution
findings.description: How access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection requests are received, decided, executed and evidenced, including lawful refusal.

layers.name: Disclosure, retention and audit
layers.description: What is released to whom in what minimal form, how long data is kept, when it may be erased, and what is logged.

findings.name: Minimal disclosure projection
findings.description: Each relying party receives the narrowest projection satisfying its stated need, preferring a derived predicate over the underlying attribute, with special-category data excluded by default.

findings.name: Retention, erasure and disclosure audit
findings.description: Retention classes and periods, the tension between permanent vital records and erasure rights, the method by which deletion is demonstrated, and what every disclosure must log.

bundles.name: Quality and interoperability
bundles.description: Attribute accuracy and correction, and disciplined alignment to external vocabularies including script and transliteration handling.
bundles.rationale: Accuracy is a legal principle for personal data and a quality requirement for civil registration; alignment to external standards must be recorded as mapping rather than claimed as conformance, and name transliteration is a documented interoperability hazard in travel documents.

layers.name: Attribute quality and correction
layers.description: Provenance and freshness of each attribute, the correction pathway, and the quality indicators measured over the person population.

findings.name: Attribute accuracy and correction
findings.description: Every core attribute carries a source and last-verified time; corrections supersede rather than overwrite, and population-level quality is measured.

layers.name: External alignment and encoding
layers.description: Versioned mappings to external vocabularies and credential schemas, and script, encoding and transliteration handling for names.

findings.name: External schema alignment
findings.description: Alignments to external vocabularies are versioned, explicitly lossy where relevant, and are mappings until conformance evidence exists.

findings.name: Script, encoding and transliteration
findings.description: Names exist in native script, transliterated and machine-readable truncated forms; each form must be identified, rule-bound and reconcilable to the registered name.

model.name: Physical Item Instance
model.purpose: Model the context an agent needs to identify, describe, track and govern one individual physical thing as a distinguishable instance, separately from the type it instantiates and from any value, inventory or asset projection over it.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the individuated, one-of-a-kind record of a discrete physical thing: how it is identified and marked, which type it instantiates, what was measured on this specimen, its condition and lifecycle state, where it has been observed, who has held it, the events and provenance evidence attached to it, and the governance of that record. It excludes all class-level description, all quantity aggregation, and every concept mastered by a composable sibling model. Storage and interface (JSON, Markdown, Git, MongoDB, MCP) are projections, never semantics.
in_scope: Instance-level identifiers, identity marks, data carriers, and identifier resolution/collision handling for one physical thing
The instance-of link to a product type or configuration, and rules for identity continuity across repair, replacement and reconfiguration
Properties measured on this specimen (as-built/as-observed), distinct from type specifications
Condition, damage, intervention history and lifecycle state including end of life
Observed whereabouts (location fixes, containment context) and custody/possession records
Events, provenance, chain-of-custody and evidence/attestations attached to the individual thing
Record stewardship: mastership, access scoping, privacy, retention, audit and external alignment
out_of_scope: Type, model, design and configuration specifications (mastered by WM-OBJ-002 and WM-OBJ-017)
Material substance classes and their properties (mastered by the material substance sibling model)
Countable stock quantities and inventory positions (mastered by WM-OBJ-020)
Packaging and handling-unit structures as containers in their own right (mastered by WM-OBJ-021)
Place identity, premises geometry and address semantics (mastered by WM-BLT-002)
Financial, value and asset-management projections over the item (WM-OBJ-022 is a view, not a second master)
Legal title, ownership registration and party identity (mastered by the S1 ownership/party models)
Bulk, fungible or continuous matter with no individuating boundary, and batch/lot-level identity
Human beings, living organisms and purely digital or conceptual items
Maintenance work management, job planning and spare-part provisioning processes

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-OBJ-002 Product type / WM-OBJ-017 Product configuration
boundary_notes.distinction: Type-instance boundary. schema.org separates Product/ProductModel from IndividualProduct ('a single, identifiable product instance'), and EPCIS separates class-level identification (GTIN/LGTIN with quantity) from instance-level identification (SGTIN, SSCC). Specifications, variants and marketing attributes stay in the type models; only the resolved reference and instance-specific deviations live here.

The assembly graph, positions and build structure are mastered by WM-OBJ-012. This model carries only the membership pointer (parent item, role, installed/removed time) needed to interpret the individual, mirroring CIDOC CRM P46 is composed of and EPCIS AggregationEvent parent/child semantics.

Inventory is a quantity of a type at a location; this model never masters counts. An item instance may be referenced by a stock position, but a stock position is not decomposable into instances unless each instance is separately identified.

A handling unit (SSCC-identified logistic unit) is itself a physical thing that contains items. Containment is recorded here as observed context only; the packaging hierarchy is mastered by WM-OBJ-021.

ISO 55000 defines an asset as a thing or entity with potential or actual value to an organization; that is a value-relative role that may span portfolios, systems and non-physical entities. Asset records are a projection over this item and must not mint a second master identity.

Premises contain item instances. Place identity, geometry and hierarchy are mastered there; here only a resolved place reference plus observation quality (EPCIS readPoint vs bizLocation, CIDOC P53 has former or current location).

Instance identity requires an individuating physical boundary. ISO 22095 chain-of-custody models such as mass balance and controlled blending explicitly break one-to-one identity between input and output material, so batch/lot traceability must not be modelled as instance identity here.
Custody (holding, CIDOC P49 keeper) is modelled here; title and ownership (CIDOC P52 current owner) resolve to the ownership model, which also supplies the stewardship authority for this record.

functions.name: Register item instance
functions.description: Create the master record for one individual physical thing, binding it to an authoritative identifier and, where known, to its type.
preconditions: The candidate passes the individuation test and is not bulk, batch or fungible matter
No existing record already resolves the same identifier under the same scheme
effects: A new master record exists with record version 1 and an RFC 3339 creation timestamp
A registration event is appended to the item event stream

functions.name: Assign identifier and record identity mark
functions.description: Allocate or record an identifier for the item and register the physical mark or data carrier that bears it.
preconditions: The assigning party is authorised under the scheme's rules
The identifier is unique within the declared uniqueness scope
effects: The item carries an additional identifier and mark with an application timestamp
Superseded marks are closed with an end timestamp rather than deleted

functions.name: Resolve observed identifier to item
functions.description: Resolve a scanned, quoted or inferred identifier to at most one item record, reporting ambiguity instead of guessing.
outputs: matched item reference or empty result
ambiguity report where more than one candidate matches
preconditions: The identifier syntax is recognisable or explicitly flagged as unrecognised
effects: A resolution attempt is logged with outcome and timestamp
Multiple matches raise a collision case rather than returning an arbitrary record

functions.name: Capture item event
functions.description: Append a validated event about the item recording what happened, when, where, why and how.
preconditions: Event time is RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset
The item identifier resolves to exactly one record or the event is quarantined
effects: The event stream gains an immutable entry with both event time and record time
Derived current status, whereabouts and containment are recalculated

functions.name: Record condition assessment
functions.description: Attach a dated condition judgement to the item with scale, method, assessor and supporting evidence.
preconditions: The scale is a named, versioned scale rather than an ad hoc grade
The assessor reference resolves to a party or device
effects: Prior assessments are retained as history and not overwritten
Assessments older than the staleness threshold cease to be presented as current

functions.name: Transition lifecycle state
functions.description: Move the item to a new governed status through a permitted transition, or reject the request.
preconditions: The transition is permitted by the versioned state model
Persistent states such as recalled or stolen are not silently cleared
effects: Status and effective-from timestamp are updated and the prior status is retained in history
Terminal transitions start the record retention clock

functions.name: Transfer custody
functions.description: Close the outgoing custody period and open the incoming one, recording basis, parties and acknowledgement.
preconditions: At most one custody period is open before and after the operation
Transfer time is not earlier than the start of the custody period being closed
effects: Custody history gains a closed period and a new open period
Unacknowledged transfers are flagged for reconciliation rather than assumed complete

functions.name: Attach or detach item from assembly
functions.description: Record that the item was installed into or removed from a parent item at a stated time and position.
preconditions: The parent item resolves to an existing item record
No overlapping open membership exists for the same item
effects: Membership periods are opened or closed without altering either item's identity
Derived location of the child may be inherited from the parent while membership is open

functions.name: Verify authenticity
functions.description: Evaluate marks, carriers, tamper evidence and credentials to decide whether the physical thing is the thing the record designates.
preconditions: Credential status can be checked or the check is explicitly recorded as unavailable
effects: A verification result is appended with verifier, method and timestamp
Failures raise a case and may set a persistent state such as suspected counterfeit

functions.name: Merge or split item records
functions.description: Reconcile records after discovering that two records describe one thing, or that one record conflated two things.
preconditions: Evidence supporting sameness or difference is attached and graded
The deciding role is authorised by the mastership rules
effects: Retired records are marked superseded with a pointer to the survivor rather than deleted
Events, custody and observations are re-parented with their original provenance preserved

functions.name: Retire item and close record
functions.description: Record the item's end of life with evidence and place the record under its retention schedule.
preconditions: Evidence of the terminal event is attached or the mode is recorded as unverified
No open custody period remains, or the open period is explicitly closed as part of the operation
effects: The item is no longer presented as active in any projection
The record is retained until its retention date and then handled per the disposition action

functions.name: Issue scoped disclosure view
functions.description: Produce a projection of the record limited to a defined field set for a named audience, and log the disclosure.
preconditions: A grant, published-view definition or recorded exception authorises the disclosure
Prohibited fields for the view are enforced by the view definition, not by the caller
effects: The requesting party receives only the fields the view defines
A disclosure record is written with recipient, scope, basis and RFC 3339 timestamp

functions.name: Transform item identity
functions.description: Consume this identity and generate successor item identities when a physical transformation so requires, recording PROV derivation.
inputs: Transformation event with inputs consumed and outputs produced
outputs: Successor item identities and PROV derivation links
preconditions: Evidence supports that the transformation ended this identity rather than repairing it
effects: Consumes this identity and generates successor items
Records wasDerivedFrom links from predecessor to successors

functions.name: Bind digital representation
functions.description: Link an IL, Digital Link, DPP or AAS record to this item while keeping shell and passport identifiers distinct from the item master.
inputs: Representation kind: Identification Link, Digital Link, DPP or AAS
Representation identifiers including globalAssetId, specificAssetIds and shell id
Grain evidence for the representation identifier
preconditions: Representation identifier grain is instance-level or recorded as unspecified
effects: Links the representation to the item
Marks representation identifiers as not the item master

functions.name: Quarantine or correct statement
functions.description: Flag failed validation, cloned-serial suspicion or conflicting events without deleting history; corrections are new statements.
inputs: Failing rule id and offending fact reference
outputs: Corrective statement with its own record time
preconditions: The original statement remains readable in history
effects: Quarantines the suspect statement instead of deleting it
Adds corrections as new statements

functions.name: Report loss, theft or seizure
functions.description: Set exceptional status with last-known location and holder, without treating the item as disposed.
outputs: Exceptional status assertion and case file
preconditions: Unknown whereabouts is not recorded as non-existence
effects: Sets exceptional status while the item continues to exist
Freezes last-known location and holder for recovery use

functions.name: Recover item
functions.description: Re-enter a missing or stolen item into tracking after re-validating identity, condition and custody.
inputs: Recovery event time and recovering party
outputs: Recovery record with revalidated identity, condition and custody
preconditions: The recovered object has been matched against distinguishing features and documentation
effects: Clears exceptional status
Opens a new custody period and appends a condition assessment

functions.name: Bind kind and configuration
functions.description: Assert or revise the class and optional configuration of the instance as references to sibling masters, with confidence and history.
inputs: Class key and optional configuration id
outputs: Dated kind assertion, optionally with configuration reference
preconditions: Class and configuration masters live in sibling models and are referenced, not restated
effects: Adds a kind assertion and supersedes the prior one without erasing it
Leaves kind_status unknown or unique-object when no class resolves

composition.purpose: Resolve the instance-of link to the class the item instantiates; all type-level specification stays there.
Resolve the configured variant an item was built to, where configuration is distinguished from base type.
Assembly structure composes item instances; this model holds only the membership pointer and effective period.
Record observed containment of the item in a logistic unit without restating the packaging hierarchy.
Allow inventory to reference identified instances; quantities and stock mastership remain outside this model.
Asset-management records project value, criticality and life-cycle planning over this item; no second master identity is created.
Resolve location fixes and containment context to governed place and premises identities.
Resolve material constituents to material classes rather than restating material properties on the instance.
Supply owner, holder and steward party identities and the authority basis for every access grant over this record.

composition.target: Specialised item models (equipment, vehicle, device hardware, cultural artifact)
composition.purpose: Domain item models extend this instance core with their own semantics instead of duplicating identity, condition and custody.

composition.target: GS1 EPCIS 2.0 and Core Business Vocabulary
composition.purpose: Align event capture, business step, disposition, read point and business location semantics; alignment only, no conformance claim.
Align the resolvable expression of an instance identifier (primary key plus serial qualifier) and resolver link types.
Align the type/instance distinction and the serialNumber and itemCondition terms for web-facing publication.
Align physical-thing, identifier, condition, keeper, owner, location and composition semantics for cultural and heritage items.
Align provenance of statements about the item and the record-versus-thing distinction via specialization and attribution.
Align issuer-signed attestations, validity windows, credential status and evidence attached to the item.
Align the digital representation of an asset instance and submodel-style grouping of instance properties for industrial exchange.
Align the requirement that a machine-readable, globally unique link is attached to the individual physical unit.
Align custody terminology and make explicit which custody models preserve one-to-one identity.
Align passport payload, unique identifier and data carrier obligations where the item falls in scope of the EU regime.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name one owning package that masters item records and declare which fields are copies referenced from sibling models (type, place, party, assembly, stock).
The package must publish its identity policy: accepted identifier schemes, uniqueness scope, non-reuse guarantee and the fallback rule for locally minted identifiers.
The package must publish the versioned lifecycle state model, condition scales, disclosure view definitions and retention schedule it operates under, each with an effective-from timestamp.
The package must declare its stewardship binding to the ownership model, since every access grant over an item record derives from that authority.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one stable namespace for item instance semantics (for example world.physicalItem) with bundle-level sub-namespaces mirroring the bundle identifiers. Do not create namespaces for storage projections; JSON, Markdown, Git, MongoDB and MCP bindings reuse the same namespace. External identifier namespaces (GS1 keys, ISO/IEC 15459 issuing agency codes, IEC 61406 identification links, AAS globalAssetId) are referenced, never re-minted locally.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-obj-001 with nav path NAV.PHY.OBJ.INST and domain tags PHY.OBJ.INST
Relation records to WM-OBJ-002, WM-OBJ-017, WM-OBJ-012, WM-OBJ-020, WM-OBJ-021, WM-OBJ-022 and WM-BLT-002 with their review states
Alignment register recording external standard, version, mapping strength and last validation date for each ALIGN link

canonicalization_rules: Normalise every timestamp to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; retain the original local offset alongside any UTC normalisation and never drop it.

Canonicalise identifiers to the declared canonical form per scheme, retaining alternate syntaxes (EPC URI, GS1 Digital Link URI, plain string) as derived representations rather than separate identities.
Order event and observation collections by event time, breaking ties by event identifier, so canonical serialisations are stable across projections.
Represent absent knowledge as an explicit unknown with a reason, never as a default value, an empty string or a fabricated timestamp.
patch_rules: Statements about the physical thing are appended as events; corrections create a correction event referencing the superseded event identifier and reason, and never overwrite it in place.
Record-level patches increment the record version and write an audit entry with actor, before/after values, authorisation basis and change timestamp.
Identity-affecting patches (identifier change, merge, split, continuity decision) require the authorised deciding role, attached evidence, and a documented reversal path.
Fields sourced from sibling models are refreshed by reference resolution, not by local edit; a local override must be flagged with a reason and an expiry.
compatibility_rules: Adding a bundle, layer, finding, optional data element or new code value is a minor change; removing or narrowing one, or making an element required, is a breaking change requiring a new major version.
Vocabulary and scale changes are versioned and effective-dated; historical statements keep the scale version under which they were made.
External alignments are versioned against a named standard version; a new standard version does not implicitly change local semantics until the mapping is re-validated.
Published projections keep a snapshot per publication so downstream consumers can detect divergence rather than silently receiving reinterpreted data.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier for the item (manufacturer or registry serial identity under its issuing scheme, for example a GS1 instance key or an ISO/IEC 15459 unique item identifier)
Governed global identifier or IRI (GS1 Digital Link URI, IEC 61406 identification link, AAS globalAssetId, or another registered IRI)
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded with the reason no governed identifier was available
A date, a location, a model name or a holder name is never an identifier and must not be used as a surrogate key
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All timestamps use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or 'Z'; '-00:00' is used only where the UTC instant is known but the local offset is not. Event time and record/ingestion time are stored separately and never conflated.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serialised artifacts (certificates, receipts, reports, credentials, published snapshots) are named by issuer-assigned document identifier plus issue timestamp; where the issuer assigns none, use item master identifier plus artifact type plus RFC 3339 creation timestamp plus a monotonic sequence. Serial numbers are never reused, and superseded artifacts are retained with an end timestamp.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every artifact carries a content digest, its issuer, and the time it was captured or published; artifacts referenced as evidence are immutable, and any revision is a new artifact linked to its predecessor. Digest mismatch invalidates dependent claims until re-verified.

policies: The record is not the thing: changes to the record and changes to the physical item are separate, separately timestamped and separately authorised.
No fabricated precision: unknown identity, whereabouts, custody or time is recorded as an explicit unknown with a reason, never inferred into a concrete value.
No second master: quantities, type specifications, place geometry, assembly structure, title and asset valuation are referenced from sibling models and never re-mastered here.
External standards are alignments; conformance is claimed only with test evidence recorded in the alignment register.
Instance identity is refused to matter with no individuating boundary; batch, bulk and fungible material are represented as quantities in the appropriate sibling model.
Append-only event and assessment history; corrections are new statements, not silent overwrites of event time, custody or condition.
Identifier reuse is forbidden for customer-facing GIAI and for any scheme that requires uniqueness beyond record lifetime; retirement is an embargo, not deletion of history.
Owner or delegated steward governs the record; possessing parties may add observation events but cannot rewrite title.
Public serial lookup and mandated passport fields omit location, current holder and non-mandated condition detail unless an exception applies.
Location, custody and title are references to place and party masters; they are not free-text identity of this item.

read: Reads are scoped by bundle, layer, finding or artifact; the default for parties without a grant is deny for whereabouts, custody, holder identity and condition detail.
Derived current state (status, whereabouts, containment, custody) is read as a projection over the event stream, with the deriving observation always disclosed alongside the value.
Every external read of a published projection is logged with recipient, view identifier and timestamp.
create: Creating an item record requires a passed individuation test and an identifier under an accepted scheme, or an explicit locally minted identifier with a recorded reason.
Creating a statement about the item requires an event time in RFC 3339 form and a resolvable asserting party or device.
Creation of a duplicate identifier is refused and raises a collision case rather than silently creating a second record.
update: Physical facts are updated only by appending events; derived views are recomputed, not edited.
Record metadata updates increment the record version and write an audit entry; identity-affecting updates require the authorised deciding role and attached evidence.
Vocabulary-valued fields may only take values from the declared, versioned code list in force at the statement's event time.
delete: Item records are not hard-deleted on end of life; they are transitioned to a terminal status and held under the retention schedule.
Erasure requests affecting personal data are resolved by pseudonymisation or restriction where a competing retention duty exists, with the decision and its basis recorded.
Hard deletion occurs only at retention expiry under the schedule, is performed by an authorised role, and leaves a tombstone recording the identifier, deletion time and basis.

roles.name: Item record steward
responsibilities: Accountable for the accuracy and completeness of the item record
Approves identity-affecting changes including merges, splits and continuity decisions
Maintains the binding to the ownership model that authorises access grants

roles.name: Observer or capture agent
responsibilities: Captures events, scans, sensor readings and location observations with correct event time and offset
Records observation source, device identity and precision
Flags rather than resolves contradictory observations

roles.name: Custodian or holder
responsibilities: Holds the item and acknowledges custody transfers
Reports condition at handover, loss, theft or damage
Requests and receives scoped disclosure views needed to operate the item

roles.name: Assessor or verifier
responsibilities: Performs condition assessments and authenticity verifications against named, versioned scales and methods
Issues or validates evidence and credentials with issuer, validity window and status
Records negative and inconclusive results rather than omitting them

roles.name: Access and privacy administrator
responsibilities: Defines and versions disclosure views, grants and exceptions
Operates the retention and privacy schedule and resolves erasure conflicts
Audits disclosures and correlation risk arising from publicly resolvable identifiers

roles.name: Interoperability maintainer
responsibilities: Maintains the alignment register against named external standard versions
Re-validates mappings on standard version drift and records conflicts
Governs outbound projections and detects divergence from published snapshots

access.default_rule: Deny by default outside the owning Dimension. Identity, type and lifecycle status may be exposed through an explicitly defined public view; whereabouts, containment, custody, holder identity, condition detail, evidence and provenance dossiers require an explicit, time-boxed grant derived from the ownership model.
exceptions: Lawful requests from a competent authority or a court order, recorded with the instrument reference
Theft, loss or recovery investigations, limited to the fields needed to identify and locate the item
Safety recalls and regulatory product-passport disclosure duties, limited to the mandated field set
Emergency response where withholding location or hazardous-content data would create physical risk
Verification requests by a prospective holder, limited to identity, type, lifecycle status and authenticity result
Lawful recovery, customs and court orders may obtain identity, distinguishing-feature and last-known location artifacts without owner consent where statute requires.
ESPR or other mandated passport fields are disclosed to the extent the applicable product-group rules require.
A time-bounded owner grant may allow a repairer, valuer, insurer or buyer to read identity, kind and condition without location history.
The current custodian may read operational location and condition needed to hold the object, without title instruments they do not already hold.
audit_requirements: Every access grant, use, denial and revocation is logged with party, scope, basis and RFC 3339 timestamp
Every disclosure made under an exception records the instrument or basis, the recipient and the exact field set released
Audit records are immutable, retained independently of the item record's own retention clock, and reviewable by the steward and the privacy administrator
Publication of any external projection records a content digest so later divergence can be proven
Record actor, action, scope, item id, event time of the fact if any, and record time of the access or change, in RFC 3339.
Audit identifier bind, reject, retire and reuse-check outcomes.
Audit custody and title transfers, location disclosures, exceptional access, passport issuance and any delete or erasure.
Retain audit records at least as long as identifier non-reuse horizons for the schemes in use.

read_order: AGENTS.md at the package root: identify Name, Type, Model ID and the four URLs before touching any data
Specification URL: read scope, boundaries and the bundle/layer/finding structure to learn what this model does and does not master
Storage type URL: learn the concrete projection (file tree, Git, MongoDB collection, MCP resource) and its canonicalisation rules
Interface URL: learn the read, capture, transfer and disclosure operations and their preconditions
Processes URL: learn the governed procedures for identity decisions, event correction, access grants, retention and external publication
Only then resolve sibling model references for type, place, party, assembly and stock

coverage.claim: The Claude base plus five Grok findings covers, for WM-OBJ-001, instance identification and marking, non-serial identification evidence, digital-representation binding, type/configuration/lot linkage, specimen characterisation, condition and intervention, lifecycle including exceptional loss/theft/seizure states, whereabouts, containment and custody, event dimensions and correction, provenance and evidence, and record governance, grounded in GS1 EPCIS/CBV and Digital Link, ISO/IEC 15459, ISO 55000/55001, ISO 22095, IEC 61406-1/-2, IEC 63278-1 and IDTA AAS, CIDOC CRM and ICOM Object ID, schema.org, W3C PROV-O and VC 2.0, RFC 3339 and the EU ESPR/DPP regime. This is not a claim of universal completeness: sector identification regimes, paywalled ISO clause text, ESPR article-level grain and multi-profile validation remain open and are held below.

checklist.notes: Master identifier, issuing authority, uniqueness and non-reuse, physical marks and carriers, resolution, aliases and collision handling grounded in ISO/IEC 15459-4, GS1 Digital Link 1.7.0 and IEC 61406-1.
Governed status model with permitted transitions, persistent states, end of life and record retirement, aligned to EPCIS disposition/persistentDisposition and ISO 55000 life-cycle vocabulary.
Type link, assembly membership, containment, custody, ownership reference and lineage, each pointed at the model that masters it.
Event time versus record time, explicit offsets, intervals for imprecise time and an ordering rule, grounded in RFC 3339 and EPCIS eventTime/recordTime/eventTimeZoneOffset.
Origin, chain of custody, declared gaps, disputes and statement-level attribution via PROV-O and ISO 22095.
Custody is modelled here; title is referenced to the ownership model, matching the CIDOC CRM keeper/owner split. Encumbrances are captured as references only.
Resolution rules, single-open-custody and membership constraints, duplicate detection, credential status checks and conformance-claim evidence requirements.
Deny-by-default with bundle/layer/finding/artifact scopes, defined disclosure views, enumerated exceptions and audit obligations.
Retention schedule tied to terminal events, no hard delete on end of life, erasure-versus-traceability conflict handling and tombstones at retention expiry.
Versioned alignment register with mapping strength and drift detection, outbound projections with explicit binding level, and a rule against unproven conformance claims.
Instance-of-type reference with resolution confidence, deviations and an explicit unclassified path; type semantics stay in WM-OBJ-002/WM-OBJ-017.
Assembly membership and containment modelled as periods; the assembly graph is mastered by WM-OBJ-012, and non-instance content is deliberately excluded from instance identity.
Measured properties with unit, method, instrument, uncertainty and separate measurement and record times.
Evidence grading, credential status propagation, condition staleness thresholds and recorded conflict resolution.
Location statements distinguish read point from business location and carry precision and source; place identity and geometry are referenced to WM-BLT-002.
Tamper evidence, authenticity verification, cloned-identifier handling, grant revocation and correlation risk from publicly resolvable identifiers.
Personal-data linkage assessment, lawful basis and erasure conflict handling under GDPR as described by the European Commission.
Every major finding carries an exception question: unknown status, custody gaps, contradictory fixes, verification failure, merge/split and disclosure exceptions.
Value, depreciation and criticality are asset-management projections mastered by WM-OBJ-022; ISO 55000 frames value as organisation-relative, which would create a second identity if modelled here.
Counts and stock positions are mastered by WM-OBJ-020; this model refuses to aggregate instances into quantities.
No conformance test was executed against EPCIS, AAS, Digital Link or DPP profiles in this research; all external relations are recorded as alignments only.
Vehicle VIN, medical-device UDI, aerospace serialisation and firearm marking regimes were not researched; scheme-specific constraints may add mandatory elements.

known_omissions: ISO 55000:2024, ISO 22095:2020 and ISO/IEC 15459-4:2008 are paywalled; structure was derived from ISO catalogue scope and title metadata, not from clause text, so clause-level obligations may be missed.

The EUR-Lex text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 could not be rendered by the retrieval tool in this session; all product-passport statements rest on the European Commission's Digital Product Passport page, and article-level obligations (including whether a passport binds at model, batch or item level) are unverified here.

GS1 EPCIS 2.0 and CBV 2.0 normative PDFs could not be parsed; field-level grounding comes from the GS1 linked-data reference at ref.gs1.org/epcis/, corroborated by implementation documentation, so exact clause wording is not quoted.
Sector identification regimes (VIN, UDI, aerospace and defence item unique identification, firearms marking) were not researched and may impose mandatory identity elements.
Automatic data capture technology standards (RFID air interfaces, symbol quality grading) and metrology vocabulary for uncertainty were not consulted.
Animal and plant individual identification, and identification of persons, are excluded and unresearched.
Cultural-property specific provenance and restitution regimes were not researched beyond CIDOC CRM's structural vocabulary.
ISO 15459 unique identification of transport units and items was not fetched as full text and is a likely additional identifier-scheme alignment.
FDA UDI, ISO 3779 VIN, IMEI and other sector instance keys are omitted here and belong in specialized extension models.
National property, bailment, pledge, wreck and salvage law is not modelled beyond a jurisdiction-tagged title claim.
Basel Convention waste-shipment and other disposal-law processes are not sourced.
Living organisms and specimens as biological collecting events (Darwin Core) are not sourced; natural-object admission is only via CIDOC E18 alignment.
Fine-grained condition taxonomies (museum condition reports, ISO condition-monitoring series) were not fetched.
Full CBV and EPCIS enumerations are aligned by reference; only values evidenced in the retrieved standard summaries are named locally.
ISO 55000/55001 full text beyond the official overview, asset definition and lifecycle phrasing was paywalled; detailed AMS clause mapping is a gap.
EUR-Lex HTML fetch for ESPR returned empty in this run; DPP grain and registry behaviour rely on official CELEX identity plus retrieved recitals/definitions from search of the legal text.
Insurance, valuation, customs tariff of the instance, hazardous-goods instance state and calibration status are omitted.
conflicts: Instance identity has at least four competing governed namespaces: GS1 instance keys, ISO/IEC 15459 unique item identifiers under registered issuing agencies, IEC 61406 identification links and AAS global asset identifiers. None subsumes the others, so the model must carry multiple identifiers with an explicit priority rule rather than assume one canonical scheme.

schema.org itemCondition is a commerce enumeration attached to offers, while ISO 55000 and CIDOC CRM treat condition as an assessed state over a time-span. Publishing an engineering condition grade as itemCondition would lose the assessor, method and validity window.

ISO 55000 defines an asset as a value-bearing thing or entity for an organization, which can include portfolios, systems, software and people. Treating an item record as an asset record would create a second, value-relative identity for the same physical thing.

CIDOC CRM individuates physical things as units of documentation at whatever granularity the documenting institution chooses, while EPCIS expects one instance identifier per tracked object. The same physical thing can therefore be legitimately individuated differently by two conformant systems.

ISO 22095 mass-balance and controlled-blending custody models explicitly do not preserve one-to-one identity between input and output, so a chain-of-custody claim is not evidence of instance continuity even when it accompanies a serialised product.

RFC 3339 and ISO 8601 diverge on details such as the '-00:00' unknown-offset convention, and RFC 9557 extends RFC 3339 with time zone names; systems exchanging timestamps may interpret offsets differently.
No consulted source resolves identity continuity across component replacement or rebuild, so the continuity rule is a local policy decision and not a standards-backed fact.
ISO 55000 asset (value to an organization, possibly non-physical) is not identical to a physical item instance; treating an asset register as the item master is a conflict with WM-OBJ-022 VIEW.

GS1 GIAI is assigned by the asset owner or manager and may or may not travel with the object; IEC 61406 IL is assigned by the manufacturer to a unit already given unique identity. Both may coexist; neither is universally master.
Schema.org serialNumber is unstructured text; GS1 and IEC 61406 are structured, namespaced identifiers. Alignment is semantic, not syntactic.
GRAI without serial identifies a returnable asset type; GRAI with serial identifies an instance. Using GRAI as if it were always instance-granular is a conflict.
ESPR unique product identifier may be specified at model, batch or item grain by delegated acts; binding it as an instance master without grain evidence is a conflict.
EPCIS permits class-level events; inferring instance location or custody from class events without completeness_verified is a conflict with instance mastership.
AAS globalAssetId, specificAssetId and shell id are three different identifiers; using the shell id as the physical item id is a conflict.
GIAI must not identify a trade item or logistic unit; using one physical mark as GTIN, SSCC and GIAI is a conflict.
CIDOC E22 excludes purely natural objects that this model's purpose (any individual physical thing) still admits under a broader E18 alignment.
regional_assumptions: Digital product passport, unique product identifier, data carrier and registry obligations are EU-specific under Regulation (EU) 2024/1781; the Commission's registry became operational on 20 July 2026 and battery passports are indicated as mandatory from 18 February 2027. Non-EU jurisdictions have different or no equivalent duties.
GDPR-derived privacy and retention constraints assume EEA applicability; other jurisdictions apply different lawful bases, retention rules and erasure rights.
GS1 identification is globally scoped but voluntary and licence-based; sectors and national regimes mandate other schemes, so an item may have no GS1 key at all.

Custody, title and possession distinctions assume a legal system that separates them; specific transfer formalities, restitution claims and export controls are jurisdiction-dependent and out of scope here.
Condition grading scales are industry- and market-specific; no global scale was found, so scale identity and version must always accompany a grade.
GS1 key issuance depends on GS1 Company Prefix allocation by member organisations; not all jurisdictions or informal makers participate.
EU ESPR/DPP obligations and the 19 July 2026 registry duty are regional law with extra-territorial effects on goods placed on the EU market.
Object ID recovery practice is internationally promoted (ICOM, INTERPOL, WCO, EU customs) but is not a statutory identifier in every state.
Ownership versus possession is recorded in a way compatible with both PGLN supply-chain practice and CIDOC title transfer; specific common-law or civil-law estates are not assumed.
IEC 61406 and AAS practice is strongest in industrial equipment in Europe; consumer trade items more often use GS1.
Time zones and RFC 3339 offsets are required even where local operational systems store naive local time.
adversarial_checks: Ship of Theseus: after progressive replacement of every component, does the record still designate the same item? The model forces an explicit, versioned continuity policy and lineage links instead of an implicit answer, and marks the absence of a standards-backed rule as a gap.

Fungible counterexample: five hundred identical unmarked screws must not receive instance records. The individuation test and the quantity boundary finding refuse instance identity and redirect to the stock and batch models.

Cloned identifier: two physical things presenting one serial number must not silently merge. Resolution raises a collision case, authenticity verification can set a persistent suspected-counterfeit state, and neither record is deleted.

Passport level mismatch: a digital product passport may bind at model or batch level, so its presence must never be read as proof of instance identity; the exchange finding requires the binding level to be stated explicitly.
Asset conflation: an asset register entry covering a system or portfolio must not become a second master identity for one item; WM-OBJ-022 is held as a projection.

Never-observed item: an item known to exist but never scanned must be representable without inventing a location fix; unknown whereabouts is an explicit state with a last-known observation and an escalation rule.
Clock disorder: a record time earlier than its event time, or two events with identical timestamps, must not silently reorder history; the ordering rule and anomaly flag surface it.

Erasure versus traceability: a lawful erasure request that collides with a statutory retention or product-safety duty must produce a recorded decision (erase, restrict, pseudonymise or refuse), not a silent deletion or a silent refusal.
Destroyed item with live obligations: destruction must close the item's life without deleting the record, since warranty, recall, restitution and audit duties can outlive the thing.
Cloned or reused serials: a matching identifier is not sufficient identity; Object ID distinguishing features, photographs and non-reuse checks must be able to split or dispute the binding.
Second-master attack via asset register, DPP, AAS or stock keeping unit: those records must hang off this item id, not replace it.
Lot-as-instance: a batch code or unserialised GTIN presented as an item master must be rejected or reclassified.
Handling-unit confusion: scanning an SSCC must not create or overwrite a physical-item identity.
Silent identifier recycle after disposal: GIAI non-reuse beyond record lifetime must block re-registration.
Transformation laundering: melting, splitting or kitting must either mint successor ids or be an evidenced same-identity repair, not an implicit overwrite.
Public lookup leak: serial resolution must not reveal holder or location by default.
Natural unmarked object: absence of a manufacturer serial must still allow a Dimension UID plus distinguishing-feature evidence, or the object cannot be tracked as an instance.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently classify WM-OBJ-001 as an entity and both refuse a second master identity for type, configuration, stock, handling unit, assembly, asset register, passport or shell. The base (Claude) boundary is adopted because it names the mastering sibling for every excluded concept (WM-OBJ-002/017 type and configuration, WM-OBJ-012 as-built assembly, WM-OBJ-020 stock, WM-OBJ-021 handling unit, WM-OBJ-022 asset view, WM-BLT-002 premises, S1 ownership/party) and carries an explicit finding refusing instance identity to bulk, fungible and batch matter. Grok's wider admission of natural and initially unmarked physical things is a clarification of the same boundary, not a contradiction, and is folded into the base scope statement without new nodes.

decisions.rationale: Claude names the mastering sibling model for every excluded concept, carries an explicit boundary finding refusing instance identity to quantity, batch and bulk, and completes the governance side (mastership, access, privacy and retention, vocabulary alignment, exchange projections). Grok is broader in identifier evidence but leaves title, disclosure and interoperability boundaries less pinned.
Both providers independently classify the model as an entity and both treat asset, stock, passport and shell records as views over it, so no reclassification, split or merge is warranted.

Asset register, stock position, handling unit, DPP and AAS records must hang off the item id rather than replace it. Both providers agree; the base states it with named sibling model ids, which the synthesizer should keep verbatim.

The base masters custody and references legal title to the S1 ownership and party models, matching the CIDOC P49 keeper versus P52 owner split. Accepting Grok's title-transfer finding here would mint a second master for title inside an instance model and contradict the accepted boundary.

decisions.disposition: accepted as scope clarification, no new node
decisions.rationale: Grok explicitly admits natural physical things and later-marked objects under a broad CIDOC E18 alignment, where the base is silent and excludes only living organisms. This is a clarification of the same boundary and belongs in the base scope statement rather than in new structure.

Object ID distinguishing features, inscriptions and photographs identify objects with no serial, an illegible mark or a cloned serial. The base covers mark durability and downstream authenticity but has no finding mastering identification evidence itself.

AAS globalAssetId, specificAssetId and shell id are three different identifiers, and IL and DPP identifiers are links to the item, not the item. The base records this only as a conflict note; Grok supplies primary AAS, IEC 61406 and ESPR evidence.

Missing, stolen, seized, disputed and deaccessioned are custody and status facts, not end of life. The base conflates loss and theft with disposal, which would let an unrecovered item be treated as ceasing to exist.

The base refuses batch identity but records no lot-of-origin link or instance-level master data such as ILMD expiration. Recording lot membership as provenance strengthens rather than weakens the instance boundary.

Event type taxonomy, the How/sensor dimension and the instance-versus-class grain check are absent from the base capture-and-correction finding, and class-level inference without verified completeness is a direct threat to instance mastership.

Title, subject, date or period and maker overlap the base measured-attributes, material-content and origin-provenance findings once distinguishing features are accepted separately. Adding it would duplicate three existing findings; the cultural-description gap is recorded for later research instead.

The base master-identifier finding already asks for issuing authority and the uniqueness and non-reuse guarantee with its period. Identifier retirement and post-disposal embargo is a question-level enrichment that needs ISO/IEC 15459 and GS1 General Specifications clause text before it earns its own node.

The base identity-continuity finding already masters what preserves or terminates identity and how lineage is recorded. Grok's contribution is evidentiary - EPCIS TransformationEvent and PROV wasDerivedFrom - and should be added as source grounding, not as a competing finding.

decisions.disposition: rejected as node, held as local policy
decisions.rationale: Grok's ordering of master-system id, governed global id, then locally minted UUID duplicates the base master-identifier and fallback questions. No consulted standard establishes precedence between GS1, ISO/IEC 15459, IEC 61406 and AAS namespaces, so any priority rule must be published as a local decision, not a sourced fact.

The base lifecycle-status finding already cites EPCIS disposition and persistentDisposition, asks which states survive later events and who may clear them, and adds permitted-transition constraints that Grok's version lacks.

decisions.concept: Public serial lookup and passport view
decisions.rationale: The base access-disclosure finding defines the public view field set and its exclusions, and exchange-projection governs passport payloads and binding level. Grok's constrained-disclosure finding restates both without adding evidence.

publicationHolds: Source verification hold: every accepted source URL, organisation, version pin and access date must be re-fetched and confirmed live before publication, including the two providers' divergent GS1 endpoints (ref.gs1.org/epcis/ versus ref.gs1.org/standards/epcis/ and /standards/cbv/) and the two IEC 61406-1 webstore URLs.

Multi-profile validation hold: the merged structure has not been exercised against distinct domain profiles - serialised industrial equipment, consumer trade items, cultural and museum objects, unmarked natural specimens, and logistics handling-unit contexts - so profile-specific mandatory elements may still be missing.

Paywalled clause text hold: ISO 55000:2024, ISO 55001:2024, ISO 22095:2020 and ISO/IEC 15459-4 were grounded from catalogue and overview metadata only in both runs; clause-level obligations on asset lifecycle, chain-of-custody models and unique item identifiers remain unverified.

ESPR/DPP grain hold: both providers failed to render the EUR-Lex text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, so whether the unique product identifier binds at model, batch or item level, and the registry and data-carrier duties, rest on secondary summaries and must not be published as article-level facts.

EPCIS and CBV normative text hold: the base grounded EPCIS/CBV fields from the GS1 linked-data reference corroborated by a tier-3 implementation site; CBV vocabulary claims carried by the accepted event-dimensions finding must be reconciled against the ratified EPCIS 2.0 and CBV 2.0 standards before publication.

Local-policy labelling hold: identifier precedence across GS1, ISO/IEC 15459, IEC 61406 and AAS namespaces, and the identity-continuity rule across component replacement and rebuild, are unresolved by every consulted source and must be published as explicitly local decisions rather than standards-backed facts.
deferredResearch: Sector-specific instance identification regimes omitted by both providers - ISO 3779 VIN, medical device UDI, IMEI, aerospace and defence item unique identification, and firearms marking - which may impose mandatory identity elements on the instance-identification layer.

ISO/IEC 15459 series clause text and GS1 General Specifications 8.0.0 provisions on issuing agencies, non-reuse periods and identifier retirement, to decide whether identifier issuance and post-disposal embargo deserves its own finding beside master-identifier.

EPCIS TransformationEvent and PROV wasDerivedFrom grounding for the base identity-continuity finding, plus CBV completeness_verified versus completeness_inferred for containment-context, as evidence enrichment rather than new nodes.

ICOM Object ID descriptive categories (title, subject, date or period, maker) and museum condition-report taxonomies, to test whether cultural descriptive identity is a distinct facet of the observed-properties layer or remains covered by measured-attributes and origin-provenance.
Darwin Core and biological collecting-event practice for natural specimens taken into tracking, since natural-object admission currently rests only on a broad CIDOC E18 alignment.
Automatic data capture standards (RFID air interfaces, 2D symbol quality grading) and metrology vocabulary for measurement uncertainty, both unconsulted in either run.

Deaccession, forfeiture, salvage and waste-shipment regimes (including Basel Convention) that govern the accepted exceptional-states and end-of-life findings in jurisdictions beyond the EU assumptions already recorded.
